2. The respondent Nos. 1-3 hereof as plain-tiffs filed Title Suit No. 106 of 2001 in the court of Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayanganj, against the appellant hereof as defendant No. 1 and the respondent Nos. 4-6 hereof as defendant Nos. 2-4, praying for declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 is illegal, not valid, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending, amongst others that in the C.S. record the suit plot was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 392 in the name Chitu Mia (8 annas) Afsin Matbar (4 annas) and Babar All (4 annas), which they were owning and possessing as such and that the suit plot No. 752 consists of 27 decimals land, which on mutual partition said Afsin Matbar and Babar Ali have been possessing exclusively in open assertion of their right, title and interest therein and subsequently said suit plot of 27 decimals fell in the saham of Afsin Matbar on a subsequent mutual partition and while said Afsin Matbar was thus owning and possessing he died leaving behind two sons, four daughters and one wife, who inherited the property and were possessing and enjoying in ejmali and thereafter an amicable partition vide deed dated 12.11.1980 the suit land measuring 27 decimals fell in the saham of three daughters of Afsin Matbar and the husband and two sons of Kuti Bibi, another (laughter of Afsin Matbar (since deceased), and they were thus owning, possessing and enjoying the said property in ejmali and thereafter they sold out the suit land on different dates to plaintiff No. 1 (9 decimals), the defendant No. 2 (9 decimals) and defendant No. 3 (9 decimals), vide registered sale deeds and accordingly the plaintiffs mutated their names and were playing Government's rates and charges against receipt since their purchases in 1984 and that during S.A. survey operation the suit plot was wrongly recorded in the name of Sultan Mia and that the defendant No. 1, being son of Sultan Mia, taking advantage of said wrong recording in the S.A. Khatian, on 5.3.1999 tried to forcibly enter into the suit land but became unsuccessful being resisted by other plaintiffs' men and hence the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 55 of 1999 for permanent injunction against the defendant No. 1 and his son Kazi Masum in the court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj, which on contest was dismissed on the findings that earlier the defendant No. 1 got a decree in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 declaring his title on the suit land. 

 3. The suit was filed challenging the wrong recording of the Khatian published in the name of Mosammat Daulat Bibi, Sukuri Bibi, Sonai Bibi and Rahela but the present plaintiffs were not made party therein and the suit was decreed ex-parte, inspire of the fact that Sukuri Bibi @ Kuti Bibi died in the year 1974, Daulat Bibi died in the year 1982 and Rahela died in the year 1984 and that Sonai Bibi was then 'residing at a different place, other then the address which was mentioned in the plaint of the Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 and thus on the basis of false report as to service of summons, the suit was made ready for hearing and was decreed ex-parte and that the cause of action for the instant suit arose when the Title Suit No. 55 of 1999 was dismissed on the ground of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998. The instant Title- Suit No. 106 of 2001 being dismissed on contest and being aggrieved there against the respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 hereof preferred Title Appeal No. 173 of 2004 before the District Judge, Narayanganj, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayanganj, by the Judgment and decree dated 24.4.2006 allowing the appeal, setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the Court below, and declaring that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 was obtained fraudulently and illegal, not valid and not binding upon the plaintiff- appellants holding,  amongst others, that the suit was decreed against dead persons namely Sukuri Bibi, Rahela and Daulat Bibi, and being aggrieved there-against the defendant respondent No. 1 as petitioner preferred Civil Revision No. 1760 of 2006 in the High Court Division, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, and a Rule was issued thereon which has been disposed of by the impugned judgment and order dated 5.3.2008, discharging the Rule without any order as to costs, observing that the summons in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 were also not duly served. Now the said defendant No. 1 as appellant has come up with the instant leave petition. 

 4. Perused the' leave petition as well as the judgments of the Court below and heard the learned Advocate. It appears though P.Ws. 1, 2, 3, and 5 have categorically stated about the dated of Kuti Bibi, Rahela and Daulat Bibi in the year 1984 and about the non-service of summons of Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 upon the said persons, who were defendants in the suit, the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the instant suit being Title Suit No. 106 of 2001, relying on the decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998. It appears that the Appellate Court below on due consideration of the evidences on record allowed the appeal holding that the suit as framed and filed is maintainable inasmuch as in the suit a prayer was made for declaring that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 was illegal, fraudulent and not binding upon plaintiffs and therefore dismissing of the suit by the court below on the ground that "the possession and title of the plaintiffs were not proved" was not proper. The High Court Division in discharging the Rule has observed that the Appellate Court below carefully and clearly discussed the evidences on record and after proper assessment of the evidences on record came to its finding that the plaintiffs by producing the title deeds and Khatians as well as the oral evidences proved their case of title and possession and that in view of the settled principle of law that in exercising revisional power the finding of facts, whether concurrent or not, arrived at 'by the appellate court is final, unless it could be shown to be manifestly perverse. The High Court Division relying on the decision in the case of Khurshid Ali and others Vs. Noorjahan Bewa And others, reported in 15 BID (AD) 82, and in the case of Hazari Bala Sana and another Vs. Niron alias Niranjan Mandal and other, reported in 17 BLD (A1))295, wherein their lord-ships of the Appellate Division have held that finding of facts by the appellate court should not be disturbed unless those were found to be perverse and or there is non-consideration or misreading of the material evidences on record, which in the instant case has been found to be absent by the Revisional Court. The decision with observations given by the High Court Division appears to be in accordance with law and no interference is called for.
